transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too, doctor. Um... I guess I'm here because I want to do the right thing and get back on track, but... well, I hope I explain this okay. I've just kind of stopped caring about things? 

I feel terrible admitting it, because I know I should be doing more, but I used to love my art classes, and going to board-game nights, and hiking. I was even supposed to be getting back on my soccer team. But lately, I just... I don't care about any of it anymore. I mostly just sit in my room and let everything sort of... slip away. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really lazy of me. Is that... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you need to know?
{"intent":"Determine how long the loss of interest and motivation has been present","question":"How long have you been feeling this way?""}

Um... well, I know I probably should have come in to see someone a lot sooner. I really meant to, I promise. But... it's been a little while now. I think it started shortly after my divorce, so... about a year and eleven months now? 

I feel so embarrassed saying that out loud, like I should have bounced back by now, you know? I really have tried to snap out of it, I don't want you to think I've just been giving up this whole time. Is that... is it okay that I waited this long to get help? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of timeline.
During this time, have you felt sad, down, or hopeless most of the day on most days?

Um... yes, I think so. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should be more positive, and I really do try to count my blessings. But... well, most days I just wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It just kind of sits there. And it feels like... like there’s no future for me beyond the apartment walls. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic and self-pitying. I really don't want to be a burden or sound like I'm just complaining. I try to push past it, I really do. Am I... am I explaining that okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
How has your energy been during this period?

Um... my energy? Well, I know I shouldn't complain, because I really don't do much during the day, so I shouldn't be tired. But... I don't know, it just feels like my battery is always on empty? 

I feel so guilty even saying this, but even if I've been in bed for half the day, just... just getting up to take a shower or answering a single text message makes me feel like I've just worked a full shift. It takes everything out of me. I really try to push through it, I promise I'm not just trying to be lazy. I want to have more energy. Does that... does that make sense? Is that a normal thing to feel when you're going through this?
Have you noticed any significant change in your sleep since these symptoms began?

Um... well, my sleep hasn't been great, to be honest. I really hope it's just stress or something, and I know I should be managing it better. I try all the sleep hygiene things, you know? But... I usually end up lying awake for hours. 

I just... I get kind of worked up, I guess? I find myself checking the door a lot, making sure it's locked, and just... listening. For things. I know it sounds silly and paranoid, and I'm sure there's nothing there, but I just can't seem to turn my brain off. And then, when I finally do fall asleep, I end up waking up way before dawn. I wake up shaking, and I just... I can't get back under the covers or go back to sleep. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the normal kind of insomnia you usually hear about. Is it... is it okay that I'm sleeping like that? I'm really trying to get better rest, I promise.
Have you had thoughts about dying or killing yourself?

Um... oh. That's... that's a hard question. I really don't want to worry you, or make it sound like I'm... like I'm not trying to get better. I know I have things to be grateful for, I really do. 

But... well... I guess I have been having these thoughts. Just... thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up anymore. I wouldn't actually do anything, I promise! I don't want to be a bother to anyone. But... my friend, she came over the other day, and... she found me just sitting there. And I guess I was saying out loud that I just couldn't keep living like this. I was so embarrassed that she heard me, I didn't mean to upset her. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably a really bad thing to admit. I know I need to be stronger than that. Are you... are you mad at me for saying that? I really am trying to hold on, I promise.
Have you made a specific plan to kill yourself or taken any steps toward carrying one out?

No, no, I promise I haven't made any plans. I really haven't taken any steps or... or done anything like that. I know I just said those things about... about not wanting to wake up, and I know my friend heard me saying I couldn't keep living like this, but... but that's really as far as it goes. 

I would never actually do anything to hurt myself, I swear. I know it's wrong to even think those things, and I'm really trying to push them out of my head. I just... I get so overwhelmed sometimes, and those thoughts just sort of slip in. But I haven't bought anything, or written anything down, or... anything bad like that. I'm safe, I promise. You believe me, right? I really am trying my best to stay safe.
Since these symptoms began, have you had any period when you felt essentially back to your usual self for at least two months?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wish I could say yes, because I know I should be bouncing back better than this. I really want to be back to normal, I do. 

But... no, it's just been sort of... continuous, I guess? I haven't really had a break from it all for that long. Maybe a day or two where I feel a little lighter, and I try so hard to hold onto that, but... it always just slides right back into the bad stuff. I haven't had a whole two months of feeling like my old self since this all started. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably frustrating to hear. I know I should be making more progress. Is it... is it okay that it's been going on this long? I really am trying to get back on track, I promise.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions during this period?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I think my concentration is mostly okay. I try really hard to stay focused on things, like... like when I'm watching TV or trying to read a little bit. 

I guess sometimes my mind wanders, but that's normal, right? Everyone gets a little distracted sometimes. I don't think it's anything too bad, or anything you need to worry about. I can still make choices and everything, like what to eat or... or what to wear. 

I really try to keep my mind sharp. I hope that's the right answer... I don't want to sound like I'm completely falling apart. I'm doing okay with that part, really.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to carry out your usual daily responsibilities?

Um... well, I guess they've gotten in the way a little bit. I mean, I try really hard to keep up with everything, I do. But... I haven't been taking any of my freelance art-education jobs lately. I just... I didn't want to let anyone down if I couldn't finish the work, you know? It's better to just take a little break, right?

And I guess I haven't been going to my community events or playing soccer recently. I just haven't had the energy, but I'm sure I'll get back to it soon. 

My friend has been coming over a lot to help me out. She's so sweet. She just... she checks on me to make sure I'm eating and showering and... and staying safe. I know I should be doing all of that on my own, and I feel terrible that she has to check on me. I'm really trying to get better at doing it myself, I promise. I don't want to be a burden on anyone. Is it... is it bad that I need her help right now? I'm trying to fix it, really.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual, or feeling unusually restless and unable to sit still?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but I guess my energy just sort of... fluctuates. 

Like, sometimes I feel a little restless, so I'll just walk around the apartment a bit. Just, you know, from the kitchen to the window and back. Sometimes I do it for a while, just until my legs start to ache a little, but I think that's just because I need to get some steps in since I'm not playing soccer right now. That's a healthy thing to do, right? Keeping moving?

But then... other days, I guess I do move a bit slower. Like, just making a cup of coffee can feel so heavy... almost like I'm trying to lift wet cement or something. It takes me a lot longer to get things done on those days. 

I really try to fight through it, though. I know I should be more consistent. I'm sorry if that sounds strange... is it okay that my body feels like that sometimes? I'm trying my best to stay active when I can.
Have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or weight since these symptoms began?

Um... well, maybe a little bit, but I'm trying to make sure I eat when I can. I mean, I know it's important to keep my strength up. 

I guess I do go most of the day without eating sometimes, but it's just because... well, lately food just kind of tastes like cardboard to me. It's hard to force it down when it doesn't taste like anything, you know? But I really do try to have something, even if it's small. 

I might have lost a little weight, but it's probably nothing to worry about. My jeans have gotten pretty loose... I've had to start knotting the waistband just to keep them up. But that's just a temporary thing, right? I'm sure my appetite will come back soon. I don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose or anything. I know I need to eat better, and I'm really going to try to focus on that. Is... is it normal for food to taste like that sometimes?
